title: Potassium accumulates at the bases of cilia and flagella

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Potassium accumulates at the bases of cilia and flagella

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Ciliate and flagellate cells show a characteristic accumulation of potassium at and near the base of their cilia, which accounts (through weakened surface tension) for the small protuberance where a flagellum arises and the ridge at the base of a row of cilia.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VI: A Note on Adsorption

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In the case of ciliate or flagellate cells, there is to be found a characteristic accumulation of potassium at and near the base of the cilia.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VI, “A Note on Adsorption”; topic “Potassium concentration and weakened tension”. Scope: ciliated and flagellated cells, e.g. Vorticella and monads

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch06-08: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The spatial enrichment claim is directly measurable and potentially discriminating. Existing public images describe basal morphology but generally lack validated potassium maps, leaving the central empirical variable unavailable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify potassium at basal bodies and compare it with nearby cortex, then test whether enrichment predicts flagellar protuberances or ciliary ridges independently of basal-body proteins.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ion-specific localization at ciliary bases is rarely archived.

Static colocalization would not establish that potassium causes weakened tension.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Basal potassium enrichment is a local, measurable pattern, and the morphological ridge at a ciliary row is visible in existing micrographs. The potassium half of the observation is not available as open, spatially registered data for the stated cells. Reanalysis of published plates would not replace a modern survey.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify potassium within a defined distance of ciliary and flagellar bases in ciliates and flagellates, and compare that zone with the rest of the cortex. A repeated basal enrichment, lined up with the basal ridge or flagellar protuberance, would support the empirical claim; a flat cortical potassium field would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Elemental or indicator maps of Vorticella and monads are not deposited as a reusable public set.

Basal bodies concentrate many ions and proteins, so a potassium peak would not by itself establish weakened surface tension.
